summary: A 1961 R-6 side-hill lookout in the Deschutes National Forest that replaced a 1933-34 L-5 cabin and is still staffed by volunteers and rented off-season.

facts.design: R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on 21-foot treated timber tower

staffing.status: staffed in summer by Forest Service volunteers

access.note: rented off-season via Recreation.gov; staffed by volunteers in fire season

visit.trail_note: reached via Forest Roads 11/1150/1154/1140 and a spur road from Sisters; early/late season may need high-clearance 4WD

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service - Deschutes National Forest, Sisters Ranger District

events.note: first lookout, a Standard L-5 10x10 cabin classified as an emergency station, finished per NHLR ('1934'); firelookout.com dates this earlier structure to 'about 1933'
current 15x15 R-6 flattop with catwalk built on a 21-foot timber tower, a quarter mile northwest of the ridgetop
registered December 1, 1998 as US 287, nominated by Marilyn Anderson

evidence.supports: side-hill site description, 1934 L-5 first lookout, 1961 R-6 replacement, volunteer staffing
evidence.quote: The first lookout was a Standard L-5 10x10 finished in 1934 and was classified as an emergency station. The current 15' x 15' R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 21' timber tower was constructed in 1961 and is regularly staffed by volunteers.
Date Registered December 1, 1998 Nominated by Marilyn Anderson

evidence.supports: rental seasons, volunteer staffing in summer, access road conditions, no water on site
evidence.quote: Green Ridge Lookout is available for rent early May - June and mid September - mid November. During the summer months, the lookout is staffed with Forest Service volunteers who help with forest fire detection.

evidence.supports: high-clearance 4WD needed early/late season; delayed opening if snow blocks access
evidence.quote: Early and late season travel may require high clearance four-wheel drive vehicles. If snow blocks access to the facility during the early season, opening may be delayed.

evidence.supports: L-5 cab location 500 feet below present tower, developed about 1933, 1961 R-6 construction a quarter mile northwest of ridgetop
evidence.quote: Developed about 1933 with an L-5 cab located 500' below the present tower, this 20' treated timber R-6 flat was constructed in 1961 1/4 mile northwest of the ridgetop at an unusual sidehill location.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the first L-5 cabin to 1934 ('finished in 1934'); firelookout.com says 'developed about 1933.' Both are treated as approximate since this is the superseded original structure, not the current tower.

notes_for_editor: A 2014 Country Roads magazine PDF is linked from the NHLR page (not fetched here, within budget) and could add staffing-era detail if a future pass wants more depth.
